summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend powers for making Defence rules about inquiries, aviation hazards and public areas, allowing replacement instruments to use revised structures and enforcement arrangements.
The minister could declare defence aviation areas by legislative instrument, and public area by-laws could nominate strict liability offences for a standard infringement notice scheme.
Defence inquiry powers would be expressed generally, with inquiries conducted by specified tribunals and the defence inspector-general excluded because separate provisions already govern them.
changes: Defence aviation inspectors would use standard monitoring powers, modified to allow necessary compliance action.
Aviation area declarations could specify height restrictions for buildings, structures and natural obstacles.
Maximum penalties permitted in public area by-laws would rise from 5 to 10 penalty units.
People receiving infringement notices could elect to have their matters decided by a court.
summary.affected: Defence personnel, landowners in aviation areas, public area visitors, inspectors and rangers would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Gai Brodtmann
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Defence Legislation Amendment (Instrument Making) Bill 2017, which updates three 30-year-old legislative instruments—the Defence (Inquiry) Regulations 1985, Defence (Areas Control) Regulations 1989, and Defence (Public Areas) By-Laws 1987—due to sunset in April 2018, to keep them fit for purpose without significant operational changes.

speeches.speaker: Luke Hartsuyker
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Defence Act 1903 to allow instruments such as the Defence (Inquiry) Regulations 1985, Defence (Areas Control) Regulations 1989, and Defence (Public Areas) By-Laws 1987—scheduled to sunset in April 2018—to be remade with modern policy requirements, consolidated provisions, and improved consistency.
